newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela may use $2.17 bln oil bids to pay debt.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela may use $2.17 bln oil bids to pay debt.

text.p: Venezuela's Minister of Energy and Mines Erwin Arrieta suggested Friday the $2.17 billion bid this week for 18 oil field operating contracts be used to pay off debt.

"We (the Ministry) are responsible for generating these revenues, and not their application ... But I agree with PdVSA's president that the funds be used to amortize debt and meet service payments," Arrieta told reporters at Miraflores Presidential Palace.
Over 130 oil companies participated this week in Venezuela's third oil round that saw operating contracts to 18 mature fields sold to the highest bidder.
State oil company PdVSA president Luis Giusti earlier told reporters in Miraflores: "1998 is going to be a hard year to balance the accounts ... so I think the idea (of amortization) is a good one."

Markets have swirled recently on the possibility that Venezuela may restructure its international debt to help reduce service payments to 25 percent of the national budget from around currently projected levels of 40 percent.
On Thursday, credit rating agency Standard & Poor's raised Venezuela's long term debt rating to B-plus from single B.
